notes.title: Occultus Command on Sale and some updates
notes.content:
Occultus Command is on sale for the next couple of days and I also added some small changes and updates in the meantime.
Changes:
[list]
[*] Added a new weapon for Lia that is unlocked from the start, all you have to do is make it to the first weapon checkpoint.
[*] Added some more navigation tips for Level 1 (in the background).
[*] Fixed some issues with the formatting for the game over tips
[*] Fixed some issues with the alternate weapon moves not coming out as easily
[/list]

I actually have to apply these changes to the demo as well, but I'll try and get that done this weekend. I figured it's more important for the main game. So...I've seen more people play the game...I don't know why many players skip the tutorial...and then complain about the game being too hard, I mean...I guess the game is hard, but some of the complaints: stun locked, not being able to change fast enough, are actually addressed in tips, or the training mode. Either way, good luck and a big thanks to everybody who's tried their luck. 

Also, in case it's helpful, here's a how to video:
[previewyoutube=UcDX5BfCias;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Back Pain or Game Dev? I choose back pain
notes.content:
The main game is pretty much done, but I decided to add a fun little demo so everybody can check it out. I think I messed everything up setting up the demo, so....if all goes well it'll be up in a few days, if not, Steam testers will kick it back. Either way it'll go up sooner or later, and I'll put the main game up at that time as well, since I don't need to send that for review, unless I just completely messed up the store setup for my main game as well and Steam just vanishes me. Oh, and I lost 3 days' worth of work on my demo due to some crazy file corruption. I spent all day today trying to fix everything, had to go to a backup and redo a lot of it. 
I took my own advice and started doing Judo again after many years. My coach is reaaaally good, also has a sambo background, I don't think she understands that I'm just trying to stay in somewhat half-decent shape, but once I'm done with this little hobby, I'm going back to more Judo and drawing, I started on a webcomic, I'll continue to check on this game and make updates fixing any game-breaking glitches and bugs, but I think I am absolutely done with this whole indie game making thing. The way that indie gaming is going, I think there will be space for 3 types of games: AAA games, shovelware, and the very rare innovative (and well-funded) indie darling, everything else will be buried by the first two, and I think the last one will be seen less unless devs get creative with the funding. Which isn't necessarily bad, and I think funding sites for creators will do more to help indie development and innovation  than anything online stores can do. I think we're already seeing this, as some really good upcoming games have been getting lots of crowd funding.
Oh yeah and my back is jacked up, I'm sure doing Judo and sitting on a chair for long stretches of time isn't helping, although working out more is actually helping my back pain (stabilizer muscles and all that), but in the short term, I'm in a lot of pain, oh yeah and the title of this announcement makes no sense. 
So...happy new year, 2020 sucked, at least we'll get Occultus Command released in 2021 *knocks on wood.   
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36026290/404fd5203abf9af6148b12f0839482758767408f.png[/img]

notes.title: New Build uploaded
notes.content: New build, fixed a small bug that did not reflect the correct time for the countdown and also gave players a few minutes less to get to the real final level. After some more testing, other than a few more graphical assets to add, game will be pretty much done.

notes.title: Maps, ending, achievements and new level
Almost done, added maps
notes.content:
Alright...I've caved, I added maps, wife said she was getting lost, and also Mr. curator dude wanted them so...., although this added a few extra weeks of development, I figured I can at least add the map function to the first few levels, and also to the levels that have multiple entrances and routes. So... I'm not exactly sure when the next (and hopefully final) update will drop, but it will have maps, new weapons, new final level, final boss and an ending, so that's it. 
You can pull up maps by holding "up", at this point it only shows what room the player is currently at, and the overall layout of the stage, also showing what doors are "no return" doors that the player cannot come back from. Although for the linear stages it will not pull anything up, just move right or left. 
Hope everyone has a nice weekend, I'm going to be checking out the UFC fight tonight.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36026290/f4f26da855c12a16095e19d6c825098c3f624e5c.png[/img]

notes.title: Nothing but bad news
notes.content:
Just a quick update, game was supposed to get done around August, and although I have enough to release the game, I decided I wanted a better final boss, which I think I mentioned in the prior post. If there is one positive thing IMO that has come out of all this it's been my rediscovery of the joy I've gotten doing art. Which, after I am done with this I'll go back to and really try to polish my skill, as for everything else, it's been absolutely terrible doing this game.  Sure, this is a hobby, and it's better than doing nothing, but on the other hand, doing something so that no one can see or play it, also doesn't seem worth it, I probably should've just stuck to Judo and Kickboxing (not that that's currently an option with COVID so, I guess there's that). 
Either way, some curator gave my game a negative review (it's still in early access but whatever), because the game has no map and doesn't explain things. I wonder how much he's played, as there is a tutorial that explains every single move, and there's even a command list. I designed the game to where even the levels that have multiple routes, will all lead to one objective, but kudos to them, for at least writing a review. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36026290/8b6f9792d80b64579d208a2a3648b15982df4d38.png[/img]
Since the world is on fire I've been having to work weird schedules from home, while my son is going to school digitally, translation: running around the house asking me a million questions. So that means I haven't had as much time to work on the game (although I am grateful to be able to work, sending love to everybody suffering out there), and because it's 2020, my back and drawing hand hurt (thanks Army). Either way, I'll probably get things done around September, I'm hoping to get a demo out, and maybe put some crazy sale to try and get some people to review it, can't wait to be done with this, so I can draw, I found a lot of great resources for artists out there, there are some youtubers doing great work with tutorials and such. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36026290/9a1cca6d34af9188a2db8ecd75de47b423ff9879.png[/img]

notes.title: Improving and still working on this!
notes.content:
Hope everyone is doing alright during these trying times. 
I'm still working on the game, in particular the final boss. The final level was not going to have this boss and I was relying on another enemy type, but it just didn't feel right. 

I was also reaching out to some youtubers, bloggers and streamers, and quite honestly, if there is any advice I have to any indie game makers is this: don't expect any coverage from anyone. Perhaps indie content is saturating the market, or the following is just not as strong anymore, either way, having a PR/marketing guy is as important as having a programmer or artist. Unless you're a hobbyist (like me), in that case, do what makes you happy!  However, this year in particular things are suuuuper tough, as many of the local indie cons and tournaments, where I was planning on showing off the game, are canceled. 
Special shout out to Klumb3r for reaching out and giving some needed coverage of my game, and also to Lord Drakkon for leaving some feedback for Occultus Command. 
Honestly, it makes me feel great that people are playing and enjoying the game, but to me the most important thing is that I'm given a chance, not every game is for everyone, and there were some valid points raised by the early playtesters, which resulted in some changes to the game. So, I'm still adding and tweaking things!
Also got some artwork for my custom stick from Focus Attack, which I think looks pretty awesome, too bad I won't be able to show it off at some cons. [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36026290/0b2eab6001e05ea160384bf1c609e1170fe5beab.jpg[/img] 

Take care and be safe!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36026290/dfc988d0e8b8355ab763ae0cde3f30af1107470f.png[/img]

Hope this message finds everyone doing alright during these trying times. I was anticipating getting this done a lot earlier but had some personal matters crop up, either way, managed to get a nice update uploaded and completed for the game and it's live now! 

Update:
[list]
[*] Added a new enemy type in Level 1
[*] Added a new boss for the Grind Hall level
[*] Added a new Weapon for Lia
[*] New moves for both Lia and Felius: the air geyser stomp
[*] New backgrounds and art!
[/list]

Game's not dead, I'm still working on some more updates to include more enemies and bosses and the final level along with a new ending. I might also tweak some of the weapons and add more animation and backgrounds. 
There was a local gaming convention that was indie friendly that I wanted to attend, but seems like that won't happen, but if you've been enjoying the game, feel free to tweet, stream or review it! Also, here's a video on how to play it. Feel free to drop me a line, message, reply to a post or whatever and I'll respond! 

Thanks.

notes.title: -40% sale let's do this!!
notes.content:
What's up commandos? We're kicking off this festive season with a 40% off sale. Get the game, play it stream it, review it, preview, hate it, love it, enjoy it for a good price, or just buy it now and play it later as I keep adding more enemies, levels and art. I might be showing my age here, but back in the days, there used to be these up-and-coming rappers that would be at airports and street corners, selling burned CD Mixtapes of their own music for about $5.99, that's me, I'm the dude with the burned CDs, except instead of music, it's a whole game.

notes.title: Devlog #2
notes.content:
Game's still got life commandos!! 
So sometime in the next couple of weeks, hopefully by the end of the month there's going to be an update to Occultus Command:
This will add two new moves per character, a new enemy type and a new boss, with a few new small areas.
I'm having to pack up and move to a new place, and moving sucks, plus my new internet provider is the one with the data cap, but on the bright side I'll have more space to breath and work on the game once the move is complete.
I also got a new computer, so now I'm able to upload more video content to show off the new updates! Once I unpack everything I'll get to work on all this. 
I have a list of some other things that I would like to add for the update after this one:
[list]
[*] more weapons;
[*] more achievements;
[*] a new level; and
[*] a new boss. 
[/list]

I'll also look into the whole remote coop play, I'll test it out and see how it works, and I might also add some more keyboard and controller configurations as well as beefing up the tutorial and hints. 
I'll try and add at least two more updates after this one, then play it by ear and see how it's received.

notes.title: Devlog
notes.content:
What's up commandos? 
I've been lurking about, and keeping an eye out for any reviews, suggestions, comments and error reports. Slow day on that front, but I've been staying busy working on the "Candela" version. 
After reading a few of the curator reviews, I've decided to beef up the combat by adding a new kind of attack
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36026290/3239c8860d34375c6f6a8883a4da35d36455a278.png[/img]
It's a slower, but heavier hitting attack, for now I'm leaning towards balancing it by making it have some recovery after the move comes out, of course that could always change, I could also make it use meter, but we'll see. I'll also have to adjust some of the enemy behavior to account for the new moves, and I'll keep these new moves in mind while working on the new enemies. 
Hope everyone is having a good month, I'll try and keep the devlogs coming at least every couple of weeks or whenever I hit a major milestone, just wanted ya'lls to know that there's still life in this game. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36026290/fa81a5db8a1f60c01b6e3f4d10c504df0b78f079.png[/img]

notes.title: Occultus Command is out!
notes.content:
Good Afternoon Commandos!

Occultus Command is officially available as an Early Access title on Steam. I will keep an eye on comments, reviews, and feedback! While I did test the game, and also had about a dozen other people test it as well, I know all too well that Murphy is always lurking around every corner ready to apply his law, so I'll stay active and keep everyone posted on any bug fixes, updates, etc.
I also plan on releasing some video updates every couple of weeks on how the process is going for the final version, and what changes, additions, fixes are being done. If you guys don't prefer the video updates, then I can stick to written announcements.
Thanks to everyone who purchased, reviewed it positive, negative or indifferent, I appreciate all coverage. So if you would like to stream, upload gameplay videos, blog, etc. you're more than welcome. I am especially curious as to how the difficulty is received, since I've gotten feedback that the game is too easy, and that it's too hard, which I find interesting. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36026290/f8a8ea298ad8f4bdb01042d535a3ee3e3a5117d9.png[/img]
